# automox_policy_file (Resource)

A file attached to a worklet policy — an installer, or a script the worklet calls.

Automox provides no way to read a file's contents back, so Terraform cannot detect that a file was edited outside Terraform. It tracks the content hash of what it uploaded instead: changing `content` in configuration replaces the file, but a change made in the Automox console is invisible.

Every attribute forces replacement. Automox rejects a second upload under an existing filename with "A file with that name already exists", so a change is a delete followed by an upload either way — Terraform does it explicitly rather than pretending to update in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A file a worklet needs at run time — an installer, or a script it calls.

resource "automox_policy_file" "installer" {
  policy_id = automox_policy.disk_space_check.id
  filename  = "collect.ps1"
  content   = file("${path.module}/scripts/collect.ps1")
}

# Automox cannot return a file's contents, so Terraform records the hash of what
# it uploaded. Changing `content` replaces the file; a change made in the Automox
# console is invisible to Terraform.
output "installer_hash" {
  value = automox_policy_file.installer.content_sha256
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) The file's contents. Stored in Terraform state in plaintext, like any configured attribute, so treat a script here the same way you would treat the worklet source in `automox_policy`.
- `filename` (String) The name the file is stored under. Must be unique within the policy.
- `policy_id` (Number) The worklet policy this file belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) SHA-256 of the uploaded content. Recorded because the contents cannot be read back, so this is the only evidence of what was uploaded.
- `size` (Number) Size in bytes, as Automox recorded it.
- `uuid` (String) Automox's identifier for the file. The `id` field this API also returns is always null and is not exposed.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Policy files cannot be imported. Automox provides no way to read a file's
# contents back, so an imported resource could never populate `content` and
# every subsequent plan would propose replacing the file. Upload it through
# Terraform instead, or delete it in the console first.
```
